name: Laennec monaural stethoscope and mediate auscultation
summary: Laennec's wooden tube for listening to the chest, published in Paris in 1819, was being used by John Forbes in an English dispensary by 1822.
description: Laennec’s monaural stethoscope used to listen to sounds of the chest for diagnosis by mediate auscultation.
tier_reason: Prefer2 for the original Forbes local-use witness; current main has already broadened the identity and added1819 evidence, so do not apply this old-scope rank blindly. This is a scoped consequence judgement, not a reward for documentation or representation.

impact.note: Listening to the chest became a new diagnostic ability for physicians across many societies, with improved stethoscopes as successors; implies tier 1, above the narrower-scope reviewed tier 2.

date.basis: Year of the first edition of Laennec’s treatise according to Nantes University Library.

events.statement: Laennec’s treatise on mediate auscultation and chest diagnosis was published in Paris in 1819.
events.caveats: A publication is an awareness proxy; it does not prove any given reader read it, nor a first invention, sale or general adoption. The original 1819 scan was not obtained for this proposal.
